column9:
Trusted – One area for growth is accountability and follow-through. After managing events, Simon has sometimes shown reluctance to take ownership of the follow-up work, such as delivering content plans or maintaining momentum. These create lost opportunities. This happened for both MVRDV and AU. Increasing his commitment to these post-event tasks would help maintain the progress and relationships he builds.

One Autodesk – Simon would benefit from more engagement with the marketing side of our work and a clearer focus on agreed-upon goals. He has shown resistance to aligning with metrics or measurable outcomes (like OKRs), which makes it challenging to track his contributions. Embracing a more transparent and results-focused approach would strengthen trust and collaboration within the team - it would help planning decisions. It's difficult for me to sign off on budget without him explaining how something links back to an OKR for us. 

Brave – Finally, it's important for Simon to be willing to disagree and commit when decisions are made. While it’s healthy to voice differing opinions, he needs to support the team’s direction once a path is chosen. This will help reduce friction and create a more cohesive working environment for everyone.

Relentless - Simon often loses focus on what we are trying to achieve. He'll spend a lot of time developing a plan or proposal, but because he does not consider the OKRs or target audience effectively the plan is often off the mark. An example might be an event proposed in Norway, despite our audience being US and UK. 

Right now, it saddens me to say that Simon's work ethic, his lack of accountability, and his resistance, are causing signficant friction within the team. I believe he needs to prioritize improvements on the above areas to resolve this. Simon brings a huge amount of industry expertise - he could be a high value member of the team if he could make the necessary improvements.

column9:
One opportunity for Simon is to increase focus by being more selective about which initiatives he takes on. He often identifies many strong opportunities, but trying to pursue too many in parallel can reduce continuity and follow-through. For example, initiatives like Forma Insiders showed promise but struggled to fully take off despite significant effort over several months. Prioritizing fewer initiatives with clearer success criteria could help increase sustained impact.
Another opportunity is to apply a more data-driven, experimental mindset to assess what scales. By defining clearer hypotheses, success metrics, and evaluation points early on, Simon could more quickly identify which initiatives are driving high impact and which should be stopped or adapted. This could help him build stronger instincts for scalability while protecting his time and energy, especially given how deeply he commits to serving the community.

column8: The HOW: What behavior strengths did this person demonstrate consistently this year? Provide 1-2 specific examples. Don't forget to consider the One ORBIT Autodesk Culture Guide
column9:
Simon consistently demonstrates Relentless and Trusted behaviors in how he advocates for our users and the community. He is very strong at pinpointing initiatives that are genuinely in the best interest of the community and then grounding discussions back to what makes sense for Marketing and Autodesk as a whole. When interests are aligned, he is capable of executing high-quality, end-to-end initiatives with clear narrative value.
He is also Brave in speaking up when internal initiatives do not align with what is best for users, signaling misalignment early and constructively. This strong sense of service and user advocacy has built trust with both the community and internal partners. His persistence and commitment to quality were particularly visible in the MRDV initiative, where he went beyond execution to thoughtfully shape how the story would resonate externally.

column8: The WHAT: How has this individual made an impact and delivered results for your project/team/customers this year? Provide 1-2 specific examples.
column9:
Simon has had strong impact by actively shaping and advancing an outcome-based design narrative for Forma, using real community and industry touchpoints to demonstrate how this new way of working delivers value. He consistently focuses on creating initiatives that go beyond awareness and instead show how customers and partners are applying Forma to achieve better design outcomes.
A clear example is his work on the in-person MVRDV design contest in Oslo. Simon was instrumental in designing and driving the initiative end to end, from aligning stakeholders to shaping the story around how a highly recognized architecture firm is embracing Forma and outcome-based workflows. This resulted in an authentic, credible narrative that resonated strongly with both the community and the broader market. He also ensured the story extended beyond the event itself into LinkedIn content, contributing to several posts that achieved roughly 2x our average estimated impressions.
In addition, Simon played a key role in the PropTech Oslo event, where he created opportunities for internal teams to engage directly with the PropTech community, showcase their work, and gather meaningful feedback. He was intentional about connecting these interactions back to Forma’s outcome-based positioning and thinking through how the event narratives could be amplified through external channels like LinkedIn.
